bodies.frontal: On neonatal coronal views, find precentral cortex anterior to the central sulcus. Check adjacent planes; this sulcus may lie outside an anterior orbitofrontal view.
bodies.parietal: On neonatal coronal views near the vertex, locate postcentral cortex behind the central sulcus. The marginal cingulate sulcus helps orientation; inspect neighbouring planes.
bodies.temporal: On neonatal coronal views through the anterior fontanelle, temporal tissue lies below the Sylvian fissure. Compare adjacent planes.
bodies.occipital: On neonatal medial sagittal views, cuneus lies above the calcarine sulcus and lingual gyrus below. A posterior fontanelle window can help.
bodies.insula: On neonatal coronal and far-lateral sagittal views, find the insula deep to the lateral sulcus. Access and probe angle affect visibility.
bodies.hippocampus: On neonatal coronal views, orient to hippocampal tissue bulging into the temporal horn. Conventional ultrasound does not reliably separate its internal subfields.
bodies.superiorTemporalAnterior: On neonatal coronal views, superior temporal cortex lies below the lateral sulcus. The model's anterior division is not an ultrasound boundary.
bodies.superiorTemporalPosterior: Follow neonatal temporal cortex below the lateral sulcus across adjacent planes. Ultrasound does not establish this posterior model division or its language function.
